title: RBI Tightens System Liquidity and Insulates Rupee Amid Hardening Sovereign Yields
changed: Global borrowing costs and energy supply risks maintained upward pressure on yields this week. US 5-year mortgage rates held at 6% alongside diverging EIA fuel price outlooks and crude disruptions from Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf Coast. Fed minutes highlighted an internal debate over cooling labor markets versus persistent service inflation, while the ECB weighed Eurozone growth risks and the Bank of Japan maintained its ultra-easy stance given a widening output gap.

The Reserve Bank of India mirrored this global backdrop by raising its Liquidity Adjustment Facility rate and executing aggressive liquidity drains. Daily Variable Rate Reverse Repo auctions absorbed between ₹1.40 lakh crore and ₹2.55 lakh crore at cut-off rates up to 5.49%. Interbank call money rates traded between 5.06% and 5.36% before easing to 5.27%, while the daily minimum Cash Reserve Ratio requirement was fixed at 90% to provide short-term treasury flexibility.

To defend the exchange rate against crude oil volatility, the RBI established a dedicated dollar window for oil marketing companies to route import demand away from spot currency markets. Concurrently, the regulator restricted forward contract rebooking to curb currency speculation while easing corporate outbound remittances by removing transaction caps on online Form A2 filings.

Domestic borrowing costs hardened across tenors. The primary sovereign auction of ₹36,000 crore cleared with long-end yields reaching 7.80%, Treasury bill yields spanned 5.6% to 6.3%, and State Development Loan yields rose to 7.5%–8.0% ahead of a scheduled ₹31,200 crore multi-tenor state auction.

In regulatory and compliance shifts, SEBI eliminated the mandatory merchant banker requirement for private placements of debt by select listed issuers and introduced a standardized Credit Risk-o-Meter. At the same time, the regulator issued enforcement orders against multiple Alternative Investment Funds, the RBI shifted Non-Resident Deposit reporting to the CIMS portal, and Paytm Payments Bank was formally removed from the RBI's Second Schedule.

threads.name: RBI Liquidity Drain
threads.note: Daily VRRR auctions absorbing up to ₹2.55 lakh crore keep short-term money market rates anchored near policy ceilings. A decline in VRRR absorption amounts or lower cut-off yields will confirm an easing liquidity stance.

threads.name: Rupee Defense Architecture
threads.note: Opening a dedicated dollar window for oil importers and restricting FX forward rebooking isolates spot USD/INR from energy shocks. Increased spot market volatility during crude spikes will signal a breakdown in this intervention strategy.

threads.name: Sovereign Yield Hardening
threads.note: Primary G-sec auction cut-offs at 7.80% and state paper yields reaching 8.0% set higher benchmark borrowing costs. Bid coverage and yields in the upcoming ₹31,200 crore state auction will test institutional demand.

threads.name: Debt and AIF Oversight
threads.note: SEBI enforcement actions against private funds combined with new Credit Risk-o-Meter requirements tighten structural governance. Further regulatory orders will keep compliance mandates elevated across fund managers.
